text:
oliver: FYI ran the bring-up for reranker-v3-3B: float32 vs int8. results are noisy: int8 NDCG@10 +0.024, but MRR@1 -0.049. seems to depend on query length and candidate ties.

june: did both runs use identical candidate pools and ordering? we had subtle differences last time that looked like quantization problems.

oliver: initially no. float run used stable sort by retrieval_score, int8 got upstream shuffled ids. re-run with explicit candidate_order=retrieval_score. after that: float MRR@1=0.438 NDCG@10=0.601; int8 MRR@1=0.392 NDCG@10=0.625. gap on MRR shrunk but still present.

kai: thanks. can you share the eval command and config? also dump an example failure.

oliver: command: python eval_reranker.py --model models/reranker-v3 --quant int8 --dataset holdout_v4.jsonl --order-by retrieval_score --seed 1234 --metrics mrr@1 ndcg@5 ndcg@10. failure sample uploaded to s3://ci-artifacts/rerank/v3/fails_3165.jsonl. example query: "rotate oauth client secret" float top1 is official doc, int8 top1 is a community thread, score delta +0.02 after quant.

june: did you compare raw logits distribution? quant can compress logit variance which increases near-ties and hurts top1.

oliver: yes: float std=1.12, int8 std=0.84. also tie_count (|delta|<0.01) increased by 18% in int8.

kai: operational suggestion: try post-quant affine calibration (scale+shift) and temperature scaling on logits. also add tie_count and score-variance to bring-up dashboard so we catch this earlier.

oliver: i'll run a small calibration sweep (scale range 0.9-1.1, shift -0.03-0.03, temp 0.9-1.3) overnight and post results. adding enforce_stable_candidate_order to the checklist too.

eval-bot: scheduled calibration sweep job eb-3165001 at 04:00 UTC. metrics will land in /dash/rerank/reranker-v3/bringup/3165001.

june: great. once calibration results are in we can decide if this is an eval artifact or a real quality regression. thanks.
